structures.name: Quadriceps tendon

attachments.proximal: Converging quadriceps femoris tendon
attachments.distal: Superior pole and anterior aspect of patella

structures.primaryFunction: Transfers quadriceps pull to the patella to help extend the knee.

explanation.overview: Transfers quadriceps pull to the patella to help extend the knee.
explanation.detail: Rectus femoris and the three vasti converge into the quadriceps tendon; the patella forms the intermediate bony link before the patellar ligament reaches the tibial tuberosity.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Patellar ligament

attachments.proximal: Patellar apex and inferior border
attachments.distal: Tibial tuberosity

structures.primaryFunction: Transfers force from the patella to the tibia during active knee extension.

explanation.overview: Transfers force from the patella to the tibia during active knee extension.
explanation.detail: This strong anterior band is commonly called the patellar tendon; it continues the extensor mechanism below the patella, but its named attachments are patella and tibia.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Medial collateral ligament

attachments.proximal: Medial femoral epicondyle
attachments.distal: Medial proximal tibia, including the medial condylar region

structures.primaryFunction: Resists excessive valgus opening on the inner knee.

explanation.overview: Resists excessive valgus opening on the inner knee.
explanation.detail: The tibial collateral ligament spans femur to tibia. Its deep fibers are connected to the medial meniscus, unlike the fibular collateral ligament and lateral meniscus.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Lateral collateral ligament

attachments.proximal: Lateral femoral epicondyle
attachments.distal: Lateral aspect of fibular head

structures.primaryFunction: Resists excessive varus opening on the outer knee.

explanation.overview: Resists excessive varus opening on the outer knee.
explanation.detail: The fibular collateral ligament spans femur to fibula, not the tibia. It does not directly attach to the lateral meniscus.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Anterior cruciate ligament

attachments.proximal: Anterior intercondylar region of tibia, posterior to anterior meniscal attachment
attachments.distal: Posteromedial surface of lateral femoral condyle

structures.primaryFunction: Primarily restrains anterior translation of the tibia relative to the femur.

explanation.overview: Primarily restrains anterior translation of the tibia relative to the femur.
explanation.detail: The ACL runs superiorly, posteriorly and laterally from the anterior tibial intercondylar area to the inner-facing surface of the lateral femoral condyle; it crosses the PCL but has different attachments.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Posterior cruciate ligament

attachments.proximal: Posterior intercondylar region of tibia
attachments.distal: Anterolateral surface of medial femoral condyle

structures.primaryFunction: Primarily restrains posterior translation of the tibia relative to the femur.

explanation.overview: Primarily restrains posterior translation of the tibia relative to the femur.
explanation.detail: The PCL courses superiorly, anteriorly and medially from posterior tibia to the medial femoral condyle. Its attachment is distinct from the ACL insertion on the lateral condyle.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Medial meniscus

attachments.proximal: Anterior horn at anterior medial tibial intercondylar area
attachments.distal: Posterior horn at posterior medial tibial intercondylar area

structures.primaryFunction: Helps distribute tibiofemoral load and improves joint surface congruence.
movements: adaptation during knee flexion and extension

explanation.overview: Helps distribute tibiofemoral load and improves joint surface congruence.
explanation.detail: A more C-shaped fibrocartilage wedge between medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau. Its capsule and deep MCL connections reduce its mobility compared with the lateral meniscus.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Lateral meniscus

attachments.proximal: Anterior horn in anterior lateral tibial intercondylar area
attachments.distal: Posterior horn in posterior lateral tibial intercondylar area

structures.primaryFunction: Helps distribute tibiofemoral load and improves joint surface congruence.
movements: adaptation during knee flexion and extension

explanation.overview: Helps distribute tibiofemoral load and improves joint surface congruence.
explanation.detail: This more nearly circular fibrocartilage wedge lies on the lateral tibial plateau beneath the lateral femoral condyle. Popliteus-related posterolateral separation allows greater movement; it is not attached to the LCL.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Supraspinatus tendon

attachments.proximal: Supraspinatus muscle from supraspinous fossa
attachments.distal: Superior facet of humeral greater tubercle

structures.primaryFunction: Helps initiate shoulder abduction and maintain humeral head position.

explanation.overview: Helps initiate shoulder abduction and maintain humeral head position.
explanation.detail: The superior rotator-cuff tendon passes over the glenohumeral joint and blends with nearby cuff tissues.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Infraspinatus tendon

attachments.proximal: Infraspinatus muscle from infraspinous fossa
attachments.distal: Middle facet of humeral greater tubercle

structures.primaryFunction: Transmits infraspinatus pull for external rotation and dynamic shoulder stability.

explanation.overview: Transmits infraspinatus pull for external rotation and dynamic shoulder stability.
explanation.detail: This posterior cuff tendon attaches below the supraspinatus insertion and blends with adjacent rotator-cuff fibers.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Subscapularis tendon

attachments.proximal: Subscapularis muscle from anterior subscapular fossa
attachments.distal: Humeral lesser tubercle

structures.primaryFunction: Transmits subscapularis pull for internal rotation and anterior dynamic stability.

explanation.overview: Transmits subscapularis pull for internal rotation and anterior dynamic stability.
explanation.detail: The anterior cuff inserts on the lesser, not the greater, humeral tubercle.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Glenoid labrum

attachments.proximal: Peripheral rim of scapular glenoid cavity
attachments.distal: Circumferential fibrocartilaginous rim; no distal bony insertion
attachments.notes: Rim-like attachment rather than origin/insertion pair.

structures.primaryFunction: Deepens the glenoid socket and contributes to glenohumeral stability.

explanation.overview: Deepens the glenoid socket and contributes to glenohumeral stability.
explanation.detail: The labrum encircles the glenoid and provides an attachment region for capsuloligamentous structures and the long head of biceps.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Iliofemoral ligament

attachments.proximal: Anterior inferior iliac spine region
attachments.distal: Anterior femoral intertrochanteric line

structures.primaryFunction: Reinforces the anterior hip capsule and limits excess extension.

explanation.overview: Reinforces the anterior hip capsule and limits excess extension.
explanation.detail: The Y-shaped iliofemoral ligament connects anterior pelvis to proximal femur and contributes to upright hip restraint.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Ischiofemoral ligament

attachments.proximal: Posterior acetabular rim / ischial part of capsule
attachments.distal: Femoral neck capsule with fibers winding anteriorly toward proximal femur

structures.primaryFunction: Supports the posterior hip capsule and resists some internal rotation.

explanation.overview: Supports the posterior hip capsule and resists some internal rotation.
explanation.detail: Fibers spiral from the posterior acetabular margin around the femoral neck; precise distal fiber attachments vary by description.

unresolved: Fine distal band separation and source-to-mesh attachment landmarks require anatomical review.

structures.name: Acetabular labrum

attachments.proximal: Acetabular bony rim
attachments.distal: Circumferential fibrocartilaginous ring; no distal bony insertion
attachments.notes: Rim-like anatomy; origin/insertion convention not applicable.

structures.primaryFunction: Deepens the acetabular socket and helps maintain joint fluid sealing and stability.

explanation.overview: Deepens the acetabular socket and helps maintain joint fluid sealing and stability.
explanation.detail: The labrum attaches around the hip socket rim and interacts with the femoral head during movement; it is not a tendon spanning two bones.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Calcaneal tendon

attachments.proximal: Conjoined distal tendons of gastrocnemius and soleus
attachments.distal: Posterior calcaneal tuberosity

structures.primaryFunction: Transmits calf muscle force to the heel during plantarflexion.

explanation.overview: Transmits calf muscle force to the heel during plantarflexion.
explanation.detail: The Achilles or calcaneal tendon joins the gastrocnemius and soleus to the posterior heel.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Anterior talofibular ligament

attachments.proximal: Anterior margin of lateral malleolus (fibula)
attachments.distal: Lateral anterior talus

structures.primaryFunction: Resists anterior talar translation and inversion especially in plantarflexion.

explanation.overview: Resists anterior talar translation and inversion especially in plantarflexion.
explanation.detail: The ATFL is one component of the lateral ankle ligament complex; the posterior talofibular ligament is another component not separately inventoried in this 26-structure scope.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Calcaneofibular ligament

attachments.proximal: Distal fibula near lateral malleolus
attachments.distal: Lateral calcaneus

structures.primaryFunction: Resists inversion, including at the subtalar joint.

explanation.overview: Resists inversion, including at the subtalar joint.
explanation.detail: The CFL crosses from fibula to calcaneus and participates with the talofibular ligaments in the lateral ankle ligament complex.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Deltoid ligament complex

attachments.proximal: Medial malleolus of tibia
attachments.distal: Medial talus, calcaneus and navicular via component bands

structures.primaryFunction: Resists excessive eversion and supports the medial ankle.

explanation.overview: Resists excessive eversion and supports the medial ankle.
explanation.detail: Multiple deep and superficial bands link the medial malleolus to hindfoot and midfoot sites. The complex is not one narrow cord.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Flexor retinaculum

attachments.proximal: Scaphoid tubercle and trapezium ridge (radial attachment)
attachments.distal: Pisiform and hook of hamate (ulnar attachment)
attachments.notes: Two-sided transverse attachment, not a proximal/distal tendon.

structures.primaryFunction: Forms the palmar roof of the carpal tunnel.
movements: flexor tendon retention during wrist/finger movement

explanation.overview: Forms the palmar roof of the carpal tunnel.
explanation.detail: A transverse fibrous band anchors across the carpal arch and retains flexor tendons while the median nerve passes underneath.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Scapholunate interosseous ligament

attachments.proximal: Scaphoid
attachments.distal: Lunate

structures.primaryFunction: Couples scaphoid and lunate movement and contributes to wrist stability.

explanation.overview: Couples scaphoid and lunate movement and contributes to wrist stability.
explanation.detail: The dorsal component is especially important biomechanically; this ligament is different from the TFCC at the ulnar side of the wrist.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Triangular fibrocartilage complex

attachments.proximal: Distal radius sigmoid-notch side and associated radioulnar ligaments
attachments.distal: Ulnar fovea/styloid and neighboring ulnocarpal ligaments

structures.primaryFunction: Supports distal radioulnar stability and transmits load at the ulnar wrist.

explanation.overview: Supports distal radioulnar stability and transmits load at the ulnar wrist.
explanation.detail: The TFCC is a complex with a central articular disc and multiple supporting ligaments, not an isolated triangular piece.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Anterior longitudinal ligament

attachments.proximal: Longitudinal anterior vertebral body surface, upper cervical region
attachments.distal: Anterior vertebral bodies and discs through sacral levels

structures.primaryFunction: Limits excessive spinal extension.

explanation.overview: Limits excessive spinal extension.
explanation.detail: A broad band spans anterior vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs through the spine. Specific upper attachments vary with spinal level.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Posterior longitudinal ligament

attachments.proximal: Posterior vertebral bodies within canal, from upper cervical region
attachments.distal: Posterior vertebral bodies and discs extending toward sacrum

structures.primaryFunction: Provides posterior longitudinal support along vertebral bodies and discs.

explanation.overview: Provides posterior longitudinal support along vertebral bodies and discs.
explanation.detail: The PLL lies inside the vertebral canal behind vertebral bodies; superiorly it continues as the tectorial membrane.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Ligamentum flavum

attachments.proximal: Lamina of an adjacent superior vertebra
attachments.distal: Lamina of neighboring inferior vertebra
attachments.notes: Segmental repeated paired bands, not one continuous central ligament.

structures.primaryFunction: Resists separation of vertebral laminae during spinal flexion.

explanation.overview: Resists separation of vertebral laminae during spinal flexion.
explanation.detail: Paired yellow elastic ligaments connect adjacent laminae and form part of the posterior boundary of the spinal canal.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

structures.name: Intervertebral disc

attachments.proximal: Inferior endplate of upper vertebral body
attachments.distal: Superior endplate of adjoining vertebral body
attachments.notes: Between adjacent vertebral endplates; no disc at atlas-axis (C1–C2).

structures.primaryFunction: Distributes compressive load and permits controlled segmental motion.

explanation.overview: Distributes compressive load and permits controlled segmental motion.
explanation.detail: An annulus fibrosus surrounds a nucleus pulposus between neighboring vertebral bodies. There is no intervertebral disc at C1–C2.

unresolved: Anatomist review and patient-independent mesh attachment coordinates pending.

explorations.title: Stability
explorations.overview: The cruciate ligaments mainly restrain forward/backward tibial translation; the collateral ligaments resist excessive inward/outward joint opening.
explorations.detail: ACL: anterior tibial translation; PCL: posterior tibial translation; MCL: valgus stress; LCL: varus stress. These restraints work alongside other capsule and muscle structures.

explorations.title: Movement
explorations.overview: The quadriceps pull on the patella through their common tendon; the patellar ligament transfers that force to the tibial tuberosity to extend the knee.
explorations.detail: Together with the patella, these two tissues create the extensor mechanism. A simplified hinge animation cannot validate tendon excursion or patellar tracking.

explorations.title: Load distribution
explorations.overview: The two fibrocartilage menisci improve contact congruence and distribute load between the femur and tibia.
explorations.detail: The medial meniscus is more C-shaped and connected to the deep MCL; the lateral meniscus is more circular and comparatively mobile, without direct LCL attachment. Shock attenuation is a qualitative role, not a simulation of force reduction.

policy.purpose: Education only; not diagnosis or patient-specific anatomy
